title: The Vonindod Rises
subtitle: A Colossus of Iron and Fire Stirs in the Deep

setting.name: The Ironslag Depths
setting.description: Deep beneath the volcanic peaks of the Spine of the World, Duke Zalto's forge-kingdom of Ironslag blazes with an infernal industry that has not been seen since the ancient wars between giantkind and dragonkind. The entire complex is carved into the living rock of an active volcano, its tunnels and chambers shaped by millennia of fire giant engineering and expanded by generations of enslaved laborers who never saw daylight again. Rivers of molten rock serve as both power source and impassable defensive barrier, channeled through carved basalt aqueducts into the forges where adamantine is smelted, shaped, and hammered into components for the Vonindod — an ancient colossus of war that Zalto has spent decades reassembling from fragments scattered across the Spine of the World. The heat is omnipresent and oppressive, rising from tolerable warmth in the outer tunnels to flesh-searing intensity in the forge chambers where temperatures exceed anything surface-dwellers can endure without magical protection. The air itself is a weapon here — thick with sulfurous fumes, volcanic ash, and the acrid stench of superheated metal. Visibility shifts constantly as gouts of steam erupt from fissures in the floor and walls, and the ambient light ranges from the dull red glow of cooling lava to the blinding white-orange of active forges. The sound is equally overwhelming: the rhythmic thunder of massive hammers striking adamantine, the hiss of quenching metal, the crack of whips, and the ceaseless rumble of the volcano's geological processes echoing through every corridor. Ironslag is not merely a stronghold — it is a factory of war, a monument to fire giant ambition, and a prison for the thousands of enslaved souls who fuel its terrible purpose.
setting.atmosphere: The dominant sensation is heat — not the comfortable warmth of a hearth but the aggressive, pressing heat of standing too close to an open furnace, multiplied a hundredfold and sustained without relief. Sweat evaporates before it can form on exposed skin. Metal equipment becomes painful to touch. The air shimmers with thermal distortion, making distances deceptive and shapes uncertain. Beneath the heat lies a deep, primal fear — the awareness that the party is inside an active volcano, surrounded by beings who consider this environment comfortable and who view the party as either intruders to be destroyed or raw materials to be enslaved. The fire giants move through their domain with the casual confidence of apex predators, their footsteps shaking the ground, their voices booming off the cavern walls like artillery. The enslaved workers — dwarves, humans, orcs, and others — move with the hollow-eyed automatism of people who have abandoned hope. Their chains are forged from the same adamantine they are forced to work, and their bodies bear the burns, scars, and brands of their captors. This is a place where cruelty is industrialized and suffering is measured in tonnage.

keyLocations.name: The Slave Road
keyLocations.description: The primary approach to Ironslag follows a mountain pass that the fire giants have carved into a supply route for their forge operations. The road is wide enough for fire giant wagons — massive iron-wheeled carts pulled by teams of enslaved mammoths — and flanked on both sides by sheer cliff faces that make ambush from above nearly impossible. The surface of the road is beaten flat by the passage of giant feet and scarred by the drag marks of chain gangs. Every few miles, a waystation provides shelter for the giant patrols — crude stone buildings large enough to house a squad of fire giants and their hell hound packs. The road winds through a series of volcanic valleys where geothermal vents create pockets of extreme heat and sulfurous fog, and rockslides are a constant hazard. Near the road's terminus, a massive iron gate marks the entrance to Ironslag proper — thirty feet tall, flanked by guard towers carved from volcanic basalt, and decorated with iron reliefs depicting fire giant conquests. The gate is always guarded. Beyond it, a descending tunnel leads into the volcanic complex, and the temperature rises sharply with every step downward.
features: Volcanic fog banks provide concealment but require DC 13 Constitution saves to avoid 1d4 poison damage from sulfurous fumes each round of exposure
Waystation guard posts every 2 miles — DC 15 Perception to spot before being spotted, DC 14 Stealth (group) to bypass
Chain gang tracks and drag marks in the road surface — DC 12 Survival to read and determine patrol frequency (every 4 hours)
Geothermal vents that erupt unpredictably — DC 14 Dexterity save to avoid 2d6 fire damage when crossing active areas
A hidden mountain trail (DC 16 Perception or DC 14 Survival to find) that bypasses the main gate entirely, leading to a ventilation shaft in the outer forges
encounters: Fire giant patrol (1 fire giant CR 9, 2 hell hounds CR 3) escorting a chain gang of 12 enslaved laborers — opportunity for ambush and liberation
A mammoth-drawn supply wagon carrying raw adamantine, guarded by 2 fire giants and 4 hobgoblin overseers (CR 1/2 each) — can be ambushed for intelligence and supplies
A group of escaped slaves hiding in a volcanic cave — 3 dwarves and 2 humans who can provide detailed intelligence about the forge complex layout and guard rotations
secrets: The escaped slaves know of a secondary entrance through an old lava tube that connects to the outer forges — it is unguarded but requires navigating through an area of extreme heat (DC 15 Constitution saves every 10 minutes or take 2d6 fire damage)

One of the escaped dwarves, Brunda Ironmantle, is a former master smith who was forced to work on the Vonindod itself — she knows the colossus has a critical weakness: the control rod that connects the operator to the construct is also its power conduit, and destroying it while the Vonindod is partially activated would cause a catastrophic feedback loop
The supply wagon manifests contain detailed information about the Vonindod's construction progress — it is 90% complete, and Zalto expects to activate it within days

keyLocations.name: The Outer Forges
keyLocations.description: A sprawling network of workshops, smelting chambers, and barracks that forms the industrial perimeter of Ironslag. The outer forges are where raw materials are processed into usable components — adamantine ore is smelted in blast furnaces fueled by channeled magma, iron is shaped into structural beams and armor plating, and enchanted alloys are prepared for the more specialized work of the inner forge. The chambers are enormous by human standards — thirty-foot ceilings to accommodate fire giant workers — and filled with the deafening cacophony of industrial metalworking at a scale that defies comprehension. Enslaved dwarves and humans work in shifts that never end, operating bellows, carrying ore, and performing the precision work that fire giant hands are too large to manage. The heat in the outer forges is severe but survivable for short periods without magical protection — long enough for the enslaved workers to function, if barely. Fire giant overseers patrol the workshops with whips and brands, and hell hounds roam freely, trained to attack any slave who stops working or strays from their assigned area. Azers — fire elemental beings enslaved through binding magic — work alongside the mortal slaves, their brass-colored bodies glowing with inner heat as they perform tasks too dangerous even for fire giants.
features: Extreme heat — DC 13 Constitution saves every 30 minutes or gain 1 level of exhaustion (creatures with fire resistance are immune)
Deafening noise from the forges — Perception checks relying on hearing are made at disadvantage, but Stealth checks gain advantage due to ambient noise masking footsteps
Molten metal channels cross the floor at irregular intervals — DC 12 Acrobatics to cross safely, failure means 3d6 fire damage
Massive blast furnaces (AC 15, 50 HP) that can be sabotaged to create diversions — an exploding furnace deals 4d6 fire damage in a 20-ft radius (DC 14 Dex save for half)
Slave barracks connected by narrow passages sized for medium creatures — fire giants cannot follow the party through these tunnels
encounters: 2 fire giant overseers (CR 9 each) with 4 hell hounds (CR 3 each) patrolling the main smelting chamber — they respond to disturbances within 2 rounds
3 azers (CR 2 each) working at a specialized forge — they are enslaved and will fight for their freedom if the binding brazier controlling them is destroyed (DC 15 Arcana to identify, AC 12, 20 HP)
A sabotage opportunity: the main bellows mechanism can be destroyed (AC 18, 40 HP) to shut down the outer forges entirely, creating chaos and drawing guards away from the inner complex
secrets: The azers were bound by Duchess Brimskarda using a set of elemental binding braziers — there are three in the outer forges. Destroying all three frees 12 azers who will fight alongside the party out of gratitude, providing fire-immune allies in a fire-dominated environment

A hidden alcove behind one of the blast furnaces contains a stash of confiscated magical equipment taken from captured adventurers: a cloak of fire resistance, 2 potions of fire resistance, and a map of the inner forge marked with guard positions

The enslaved dwarves have been secretly weakening key structural supports in the outer forges — if the party triggers a collapse (DC 14 Arcana or Engineering to identify the weak points), it could seal the outer forges and prevent reinforcements from reaching the inner complex

keyLocations.name: The Adamantine Forge
keyLocations.description: The heart of Ironslag and Duke Zalto's crowning achievement — a cathedral-scale forge chamber built around the partially assembled Vonindod. The chamber is a vertical oval carved from the volcano's magma chamber, nearly three hundred feet from floor to vaulted ceiling, with rivers of molten rock flowing through carved channels that crisscross the floor like a burning grid. At the chamber's center, mounted on a massive iron scaffold, stands the Vonindod itself — a humanoid colossus of adamantine and enchanted iron that towers nearly one hundred feet from its feet to the crown of its helm. The construct is magnificent and terrifying in equal measure: its body is a masterwork of fire giant metallurgy, every joint and plate fitted with engineering precision that belies the giants' reputation for crude craftsmanship. Its chest cavity is open, exposing a hollow chamber where the control rod must be inserted to bring the colossus to life. Its eyes — enormous ruby lenses set in an iron skull — are dark, but the faintest flicker of imprisoned elemental fire dances behind them, drawing power from Maegera's prison deep below. Iron bridges span the magma channels at various heights, connecting work platforms where the final assembly is being completed. The scale is almost incomprehensible — standing at the Vonindod's feet, a human feels like an insect at the base of a cathedral spire. The heat here is extreme, the air thick with the smell of superheated metal and brimstone, and the light comes from the molten rivers below and the elemental glow of the construct itself.
features: Extreme heat — DC 15 Constitution saves every 15 minutes or gain 1 level of exhaustion (fire resistance reduces DC to 12)
Molten rock rivers (5-15 ft wide) — any creature entering takes 6d10 fire damage per round, no save; iron bridges (5-10 ft wide) span the channels at various heights
The Vonindod scaffold provides multiple elevation levels connected by ladders and walkways — 30 ft, 60 ft, and 90 ft platforms
Unstable iron bridges — some are weakened by heat stress; DC 13 Investigation to identify weak bridges, which collapse under 500+ lbs of weight
The Vonindod's chest cavity is accessible from the 60-ft platform — the control rod socket is visible inside, crackling with contained elemental energy
encounters: 2 fire giant smiths (CR 9) and 4 salamanders (CR 5) working on the Vonindod's final assembly — they fight to the death to protect the construct
Duchess Brimskarda (CR 9 fire giant with additional spellcasting: fireball 3/day, heat metal at will, wall of fire 1/day) overseeing slave operations from the 60-ft platform
6 magma mephits (CR 1/2) that erupt from the molten rivers if combat breaks out, attacking the nearest non-fire-giant creatures
secrets: The Vonindod is 95% complete but cannot be activated without the control rod, which Duke Zalto keeps in his war room — without it, the colossus is an inert statue

The elemental energy powering the Vonindod is drawn from Maegera the Dawn Titan, imprisoned far below — severing the connection (by destroying the conduit pipes, AC 16, 30 HP each, 4 pipes total) would drain the construct of power permanently, but also risks destabilizing Maegera's prison

If the party can reach the Vonindod's chest cavity and insert an object into the control rod socket, the feedback loop will damage the construct — inserting a magical weapon or item forces a DC 18 saving throw on the item or it is destroyed, but the Vonindod takes 50 points of structural damage and the elemental energy discharge deals 6d6 force damage in a 30-ft radius

keyLocations.name: Duke Zalto's War Room
keyLocations.description: Located above the Adamantine Forge chamber, accessible by a grand staircase guarded by Zalto's elite honor guard, the war room is where the Duke plans his campaign of conquest. The chamber is carved from polished obsidian, its walls lined with maps, trophies, and weapon racks holding greatswords large enough to serve as battering rams. A massive table dominates the center — a three-dimensional relief map of the Sword Coast carved from volcanic stone and enchanted with illusions that show troop movements, target cities, and projected conquest timelines. Small iron figurines representing fire giant battalions, siege engines, and the Vonindod itself are positioned across the map in formations that reveal Zalto's strategic thinking. The control rod — a six-foot shaft of adamantine inscribed with runes of elemental binding — rests in a specially constructed holder beside Zalto's throne, a chair carved from a single block of iron and heated from beneath by a magma channel so that it glows dull red. Trophy cases display the weapons and armor of those who have challenged Zalto and failed: a paladin's holy avenger, a dragon's fang, shields bearing the heraldry of a dozen fallen kingdoms. The room reeks of confidence, cruelty, and absolute certainty in the rightness of fire giant supremacy.
features: Duke Zalto's enchanted war table — DC 15 Investigation reveals complete invasion plans including timetables, troop strengths, and priority targets (Waterdeep, Neverwinter, Mithral Hall)
The control rod in its holder — removing it requires DC 16 Strength or DC 15 Sleight of Hand; triggering the holder's fire trap if failed (4d6 fire damage, DC 14 Dex save for half)
Trophy cases that can be smashed for emergency equipment (DC 12 Athletics) — contains a +1 shield, a +1 longsword, and 3 potions of fire resistance taken from previous challengers
A hidden passage behind the throne (DC 17 Perception to find) that leads to Maegera's prison below
The obsidian walls are polished to mirror-smoothness — DC 13 Perception to avoid being surprised by reflections that reveal enemies approaching from behind
encounters: Duke Zalto (CR 12 fire giant with legendary actions — see Act 3 combat details) and 2 fire giant honor guards (CR 9 each) in the war room
If the alarm has been raised, add Duchess Brimskarda (if not defeated in the Adamantine Forge) and 2 hell hounds
The control rod itself is trapped — removing it without disarming the holder (DC 16 Thieves' Tools or DC 15 Arcana) triggers an alarm that summons 2 fire giants from the forge below within 3 rounds
secrets: Zalto's war plans reveal that the Vonindod is not his endgame — it is a weapon to be presented to Surtur, the god of fire giants, as proof that Zalto deserves to rule the new Ordning. If Zalto is confronted with evidence that Surtur has not sanctioned this plan, his certainty wavers (DC 18 Persuasion to exploit this, reducing his combat effectiveness by removing one legendary resistance)

The hidden passage to Maegera's prison is Zalto's personal route for communing with the fire primordial — he draws power from Maegera's captivity, and freeing the primordial would strip Zalto of his fire immunity enhancement (reducing his fire damage resistance from immunity to resistance)
Among the trophies is a sending stone paired with one held by Countess Sansuri of the cloud giants — evidence that Sansuri has been selling intelligence to multiple giant lords, playing all sides

keyLocations.name: Maegera's Prison
keyLocations.description: Far below the Adamantine Forge, at the volcanic heart of the mountain, lies the prison of Maegera the Dawn Titan — a fire primordial of terrible power that the ancient fire giants captured and bound millennia ago to power their greatest works. The prison is a spherical chamber carved from magically reinforced adamantine, three hundred feet in diameter, its interior surface covered in binding runes that glow with a cold blue light — the only cold thing in the entire complex. At the chamber's center, suspended by chains of enchanted adamantine thicker than tree trunks, Maegera burns. The primordial is not a creature in any conventional sense — it is a living conflagration, a sentient sun compressed to the size of a house, its flames shifting through colors that have no names and radiating a heat so intense that the adamantine walls glow cherry-red despite the binding magic. The chains do not merely hold Maegera in place — they drain the primordial's energy, channeling it through conduit pipes into the forges above. Maegera's rage is palpable, a psychic pressure of pure elemental fury that presses against the mind like standing too close to an explosion that never ends. The primordial has been imprisoned for over a thousand years, and its hatred for its captors is absolute.
features: Lethal heat — DC 17 Constitution saves every round or take 2d6 fire damage; creatures with fire resistance take damage on a failed save only; fire immunity negates entirely
Adamantine binding chains (6 total) — AC 20, 50 HP each, immune to fire damage; severing 3 chains weakens the binding enough for Maegera to begin breaking free
Binding runes on the walls — DC 18 Arcana to understand the binding mechanism; disrupting the runes (DC 16 Arcana or destroying sections of wall, AC 18, 40 HP) weakens the prison
Conduit pipes (4 total) connecting Maegera to the forges above — destroying them (AC 16, 30 HP each) severs the power supply to the Vonindod and the forge complex

A control platform near the chamber entrance with levers and rune-wheels that can partially open or close the binding — DC 15 Arcana to operate safely, failure causes a surge of elemental energy (4d6 fire damage in 15-ft radius)
encounters: 2 salamanders (CR 5) and 4 magma mephits (CR 1/2) that serve as wardens, maintaining the binding runes and fighting any intruders

Maegera itself — if partially freed, the primordial's gratitude is... complicated. It is an elemental force, not a diplomatic partner. Freeing it causes a volcanic eruption that gives the party 10 rounds to escape Ironslag before the complex is destroyed
If Zalto becomes aware the party is in Maegera's prison, he personally comes to stop them — this is his ultimate line in the sand
secrets: Maegera can communicate through the flames — not in words but in emotions and images. A DC 16 Wisdom (Insight) check allows a character to understand the primordial's desires: freedom, vengeance on the fire giants, and a return to the elemental plane of fire

Freeing Maegera is the nuclear option — it destroys Ironslag, the Vonindod, and everything in the complex, but also devastates the surrounding region with volcanic eruptions that last for weeks. The party must weigh the cost of collateral damage against the certainty of stopping Zalto

A partial release is possible — opening the binding enough for Maegera to send a surge of power through the conduit pipes would overload and destroy the Vonindod without fully freeing the primordial. This requires a DC 18 Arcana check at the control platform and leaves Maegera still imprisoned but with weakened chains — a problem for another day

synopsis: The party ventures into the volcanic depths of the Spine of the World to confront Duke Zalto, the most militarily ambitious of the giant lords, and stop the completion of the Vonindod — an ancient colossus of adamantine and elemental fire that could level cities with a single step. Zalto has spent decades gathering the fragments of this war machine, enslaving thousands of dwarves, humans, and other captives to work his forges, and binding the fire primordial Maegera the Dawn Titan to power the construct's terrible engine. The Vonindod is now 95% complete, and Zalto plans to present it to Surtur as proof of his supremacy in the shattered Ordning — a bid that would place fire giants at the apex of a new giantkind hierarchy and launch a war of conquest against the entire Sword Coast. The party must infiltrate the Ironslag complex through the mountain passes where fire giant slavers march their captives, navigate the brutal outer forges where enslaved laborers toil in lethal heat, penetrate the cathedral-scale Adamantine Forge where the Vonindod stands in terrifying near-completion, and ultimately confront Zalto in his war room for the control rod that would bring the colossus to life. Multiple paths to victory exist: direct combat against the Iron Duke, sabotage of the Vonindod itself, or the desperate gambit of freeing Maegera — each with escalating consequences and costs. The third conch shell of teleportation is found here, bringing the party one step closer to the storm giant court and the ultimate confrontation with Iymrith.
hook: The intelligence is grim and urgent. From freed captives, allied giants, and intercepted communications, the picture is clear: Duke Zalto's Vonindod is nearly complete. The fire giant lord has been assembling the ancient colossus for decades, but in the chaos of the shattered Ordning, he has accelerated his timeline — enslaving entire mining communities, stripping the mountains of adamantine, and driving his forge operations day and night without rest. Refugees fleeing the Spine of the World speak of mountains that glow red at night, of tremors that shake the ground for miles, and of fire giant patrols that sweep through every settlement within a hundred miles, taking every able-bodied soul they can chain. Harshnag, if he travels with the party, grows uncharacteristically grim. 'Zalto is not like the others,' the frost giant says. 'Storvald seeks a ring. Guh seeks a meal. Zalto seeks dominion. The Vonindod was built to destroy dragons — but Zalto will turn it on everything. Cities. Armies. Mountains. He believes fire will prove his worth in the new Ordning, and he has the weapon to make good on that belief.' The party must reach Ironslag, penetrate its defenses, and stop the Vonindod before Zalto activates it. The approach is through the mountain passes of the Spine of the World — volcanic terrain patrolled by fire giant slavers and their hell hound packs.

acts.title: Act 1: The Slave Road
acts.description: The party approaches Ironslag through the volcanic mountain passes, encountering fire giant slaver patrols, liberating captives, and gathering intelligence about the forge complex. The Slave Road is both a physical gauntlet and a moral crucible — the party witnesses the human cost of Zalto's ambition firsthand and must decide how to balance stealth and speed against the imperative to free the enslaved. Freed captives provide critical intelligence about the forge layout, guard rotations, and the Vonindod's near-completion, while escaped slaves offer knowledge of hidden passages that bypass the main gate. The act culminates in the party finding a way into Ironslag proper — either through the heavily guarded main gate, a hidden ventilation shaft, or an old lava tube known only to the escaped slaves.
objectives: Navigate the volcanic mountain passes while avoiding or defeating fire giant patrols
Liberate enslaved captives and gather intelligence about Ironslag's layout and defenses
Locate a viable entry point into the forge complex — main gate, ventilation shaft, or lava tube
Learn about the Vonindod's near-completion and the existence of the control rod
Identify the escaped dwarf smith Brunda Ironmantle and learn the Vonindod's critical weakness

scenes.name: The Mountain Approach
scenes.description: The party enters the volcanic valleys of the Spine of the World, navigating terrain that grows increasingly hostile as they approach Ironslag. Geothermal vents, sulfurous fog, and rising temperatures announce the proximity of fire giant territory. The road itself bears the marks of heavy traffic — enormous bootprints, the ruts of iron-wheeled wagons, and the drag marks of chain gangs. The landscape is scarred and broken, stripped of vegetation by volcanic activity and industrial pollution, with the distant glow of Ironslag's forges painting the night sky in shades of hellish orange.
scenes.readAloud: "The path through the Spine of the World has been climbing steadily for two days, and the world has changed around you with every mile. The pine forests thinned and died miles back, replaced by scorched earth and fields of volcanic glass that crunch underfoot like broken pottery. The air is warm — unnaturally warm for this altitude — and carries a sulfurous taint that burns the back of the throat. Ahead, the valley narrows between two peaks whose slopes glow a dull, angry red through cracks in the black rock, and steam rises from vents in the valley floor in lazy spirals that catch the failing light. The road beneath your feet is unmistakable: a highway beaten flat by feet measured in yards rather than inches, rutted by wheels that must be the size of mill stones. Fresh bootprints — each one a shallow crater large enough to bathe in — march alongside drag marks that can only be chains. Many chains. The marks are recent — hours old at most. And ahead, where the valley bends between the glowing peaks, you can see it: a plume of smoke and fire rising from the mountain's heart, underlit by a forge-glow so intense it turns the clouds above to burnished copper. The sound reaches you next — a rhythmic, thunderous pounding, like the heartbeat of the mountain itself. Ironslag. You have arrived at the gates of a volcano that has been turned into a weapon."

skillChecks.success: You read the signs in the road and terrain expertly. The chain gang passed through roughly 4 hours ago — 12 to 15 captives, escorted by at least one fire giant and multiple smaller guards. A supply wagon went the other direction approximately 6 hours before that. Patrol frequency appears to be every 4 hours, giving the party a window of roughly 2 hours before the next patrol is due.
skillChecks.failure: The road shows heavy traffic, but the specific timing and composition of patrols is unclear. The party must proceed with greater caution, unable to predict when the next patrol will appear.

skillChecks.success: You identify the volcanic hazards in the valley: geothermal vents are marked by subtle discoloration in the rock and a faint hissing sound. Sulfurous fog banks are heavier than air and collect in depressions — staying on elevated ground avoids the worst of the poisonous fumes. The valley walls are unstable in several places, weakened by volcanic activity, which could be used to trigger rockslides on pursuers.
skillChecks.failure: The volcanic terrain is unfamiliar and threatening. The geothermal vents and fog banks present obstacles that must be navigated through trial and error.

skillChecks.success: You spot a side trail branching off the main road — barely visible, partially concealed by a recent lava flow. It leads upward along the valley wall toward what appears to be a natural chimney in the rock face. A ventilation shaft for the forge complex below, perhaps — an alternative entry that bypasses the main gate entirely.
skillChecks.failure: The main road appears to be the only route forward, leading directly to the heavily guarded main gate.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene sets the tone for the entire scenario. The volcanic environment should feel actively hostile — not just a backdrop but a participant in the drama. The heat, the fumes, the unstable terrain are all enemies in their own right. The evidence of slavery should be visceral and disturbing: drag marks in the road, discarded chains, a single child's shoe half-melted by a lava flow. The fire giants are not abstract villains here — their cruelty is documented in every scar on the landscape. Let the players feel the weight of what they are walking into before they encounter a single enemy. Urgala, if present, may know of the hidden mountain trail from her younger adventuring days. Harshnag will be grim and focused — he has fought fire giants before and respects their military discipline.
loot: Discarded supply manifest from a fire giant wagon (provides intelligence on forge operations and the Vonindod's assembly schedule)
A cache of abandoned equipment near the road: 2 potions of fire resistance, 50 ft of chain, a set of blacksmith's tools
Volcanic glass shards (obsidian) — worth 25 gp total to an alchemist, or can be fashioned into crude but sharp weapons

scenes.name: The Chain Gang
scenes.description: The party encounters a fire giant slaver patrol escorting a chain gang of captured laborers toward Ironslag. This is both a combat encounter and a moral decision point: the party can ambush the patrol to free the captives, attempt to follow undetected to learn more about the forge's defenses, or devise a more creative solution. Among the captives is Brunda Ironmantle, a dwarven master smith who was forced to work on the Vonindod itself and possesses critical intelligence about the colossus's construction and vulnerabilities.
scenes.readAloud: "The sound of chains reaches you before you see them. A rhythmic clinking, like a grim metronome, echoing off the valley walls and mixing with the shuffle of exhausted feet. Then they appear around a bend in the road: a column of chained captives — dwarves, humans, a pair of half-orcs — stumbling forward in a line of misery that stretches fifty feet. Their clothing is torn, their skin blistered from heat and sun, and their eyes hold the flat, defeated look of people who have stopped imagining rescue. Iron collars connect them by a single chain that runs the length of the column, each link as thick as a man's wrist. Behind and alongside them walk the overseers: four hobgoblins in scorched leather armor, carrying whips that crackle with residual heat, and two hell hounds that pace the column's flanks with red tongues lolling, eyes scanning for any slave who stumbles or slows. And at the column's head, a fire giant. She stands sixteen feet tall, her skin the color of coal, her hair a crown of literal flame, and she carries a greatsword across her shoulders like a yoke, its blade still dark with old blood. She moves with the bored confidence of someone for whom this march is routine — just another delivery. Another load of fuel for the forges. One of the dwarves near the middle of the chain — a broad-shouldered woman with a branded cheek and hands scarred from forge work — lifts her head as you watch, and her eyes, unlike the others, still burn with defiance. She has not given up. Not yet."

skillChecks.success: The party positions itself for an ambush without being detected. The hell hounds' keen senses nearly betray the party, but the sulfurous air masks their scent. The party gains a surprise round.
skillChecks.failure: One of the hell hounds catches a scent and begins barking. The fire giant does not yet see the party but shifts to a defensive stance — no surprise round, and the giant shouts a warning that will bring a second patrol within 10 rounds if combat begins.

skillChecks.success: If the party attempts a ruse — posing as merchants, travelers, or even fire giant agents — the hobgoblin overseers are fooled long enough for the party to get within melee range before combat begins. The fire giant is skeptical but does not attack immediately.
skillChecks.failure: The fire giant sees through the ruse instantly. 'You are not traders. You are not lost. You are dead.' Combat begins without surprise.

skillChecks.success: During or after combat, you break the chain gang's iron collars efficiently, freeing all captives within 2 rounds.
skillChecks.failure: The chains are fire giant make — incredibly strong. Breaking them takes 5 rounds, during which freed captives are vulnerable to fleeing hell hounds or arriving reinforcements.

combatEncounters.tactics: The fire giant fights with brutal efficiency — she targets the most dangerous-looking party member with her greatsword (two attacks, +11 to hit, 6d6+7 slashing) and uses her rock throw (range 60/240, +11 to hit, 4d10+7 bludgeoning) against ranged attackers or spellcasters. She fights near the chain gang, using the captives as implicit hostages — area of effect spells risk hitting the slaves. The hell hounds use their fire breath (15-ft cone, DC 12 Dex save, 3d6 fire damage) on clumped party members and then engage in melee. The hobgoblins focus fire with Martial Advantage, targeting isolated characters. If the fire giant drops below 30 HP, she grabs the nearest slave and threatens to crush them unless the party stands down — a bluff if the party calls it (DC 15 Insight to read), but she will follow through if she believes she is about to die.
combatEncounters.terrain: Volcanic valley road (100 ft long, 30 ft wide). Chain gang occupies the center 50 ft. Volcanic rock formations on both sides provide half cover at 40-60 ft range. A geothermal vent on the left side of the road erupts every 3 rounds (DC 13 Dex save, 2d6 fire damage, 10-ft radius). The chain connecting the captives has AC 17 and 20 HP — it can be targeted to free groups of slaves, but a missed attack risks hitting a captive.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This encounter is the emotional core of Act 1. The captives are real people with real stories, and freeing them should feel heroic and meaningful. Brunda Ironmantle is the most important NPC here — she is defiant, intelligent, and furious. She was the master smith of a dwarven hold that Zalto's forces raided, and she was kept alive specifically because her metalworking skills were too valuable to waste. She was forced to work on the Vonindod's most delicate components and knows the construct intimately. She can describe its scale, its capabilities, and most importantly, its weakness: the control rod. Play her as tough, practical, and burning with a desire for revenge that she channels into usefulness rather than recklessness. Vex Ironhand, if present, recognizes some of the captives as soldiers from units that went missing along the Sword Coast — this makes the scenario deeply personal for the companion. The hobgoblin overseers are cruel but cowardly — if the fire giant falls, they surrender or flee. The fire giant herself should be played as professionally brutal rather than sadistic — this is her job, and she does it efficiently. That efficiency is more disturbing than cruelty.
loot: Fire giant greatsword (sized for a fire giant — too large for medium creatures to wield effectively, but worth 150 gp for the materials)
4 hobgoblin scimitars and leather armor sets
A belt pouch on the fire giant containing 80 gp in mixed coins, a crude map of the Slave Road with patrol schedules, and a brass key that opens the main gate of Ironslag
2 hell hound teeth (fire-enchanted components, worth 50 gp each to an alchemist)

scenes.name: Brunda's Briefing
scenes.description: With the chain gang freed and the patrol defeated, the party can debrief Brunda Ironmantle and the other liberated captives. Brunda provides critical intelligence about Ironslag's interior, the Vonindod's construction status, the locations of key figures including Duke Zalto and Duchess Brimskarda, and the existence of Maegera's prison. The other captives provide supplementary information about guard rotations, the location of additional prisoners inside the complex, and the morale of the enslaved workforce. This scene is the strategic planning phase before the party enters Ironslag.
scenes.readAloud: "The freed captives huddle in the shelter of a volcanic outcropping, wrapped in whatever cloaks and blankets the party can spare. Most are in shock — hollow-eyed, flinching at sudden sounds, unable to fully comprehend their liberation. But Brunda Ironmantle is different. The dwarven smith sits apart from the others, her branded cheek turned toward the distant glow of Ironslag, her scarred hands clenched into fists that have not uncurled since the chains came off. When she speaks, her voice is a low rasp — damaged by months of breathing forge smoke — but steady and precise, with the focused intensity of someone who has been memorizing every detail of her captivity in preparation for exactly this moment. 'The Vonindod,' she says, and the word comes out like a curse. 'You want to know about the Vonindod. I will tell you everything, because I built parts of it with these hands, and I will see it destroyed if it is the last thing I do.' She draws a rough map in the volcanic ash with a piece of charcoal, her lines quick and sure. 'Ironslag is built in layers. The outer forges are here — that is where they process the raw materials. Below that, the Adamantine Forge — the main chamber where the Vonindod stands. And below everything, the prison.' She taps the bottom of her crude map. 'Maegera. The Dawn Titan. A fire primordial chained since before my people were born. It powers everything — the forges, the constructs, the heat itself. Zalto keeps the control rod in his war room, here.' Another tap, this one near the top of the map. 'Without the rod, the Vonindod is just a statue. With it...' She trails off, and for the first time, something like fear crosses her face. 'With it, Zalto has a weapon that could walk through Waterdeep like a man walks through a wheat field.'"

skillChecks.success: Brunda is telling the truth and withholding nothing. Her fury at Zalto is genuine and her intelligence is reliable. She has been planning for this — memorizing layouts, counting guards, timing rotations — with the methodical precision of a master craftsperson turned resistance operative.
skillChecks.failure: Brunda seems reliable, but the depth of her preparation and the precision of her intelligence are not immediately apparent. Her emotional state — fury barely contained beneath professionalism — may read as instability.

skillChecks.success: Brunda agrees to guide the party through Ironslag using a secondary entrance she discovered during her captivity — an old lava tube that connects to the outer forges. The tube is partially collapsed and requires navigating extreme heat, but it bypasses the main gate entirely.
skillChecks.failure: Brunda provides the map and intelligence but refuses to go back inside. She has done enough — she will lead the other freed captives to safety instead. The party must navigate Ironslag without a guide.

skillChecks.success: You recall lore about the Vonindod: it was built during the Thousand Year War between giants and dragons, designed specifically to hunt and destroy wyrms. The ancient version required a fire primordial to power it and a control rod attuned to a giant of royal blood to operate it. If Zalto has modified the design, there may be additional vulnerabilities in the modifications that a skilled artificer or smith could exploit.
skillChecks.failure: The Vonindod is legendary but its specific construction details are lost to history.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene is primarily roleplay and strategic planning. Brunda should be played as one of the most competent and determined NPCs the party encounters in the entire campaign — she is a master smith, a survivor, and a woman driven by righteous fury channeled into meticulous planning. She has been enslaved for months and never stopped thinking about how to bring Ironslag down. The other captives provide color and emotional weight: a human farmer from the lowlands who was taken during a raid, a pair of half-orc mercenaries who were ambushed on the road, a young dwarf apprentice who still flinches when anyone raises a hand. If the party has been traveling with Vex Ironhand, this scene becomes intensely personal — Vex may recognize some of the captives or learn that soldiers under Vex's former command were taken here. The key decision point is entry method: the main gate (with the brass key from the fire giant), the ventilation shaft (found during the Mountain Approach scene), or the lava tube (revealed by Brunda). Each has trade-offs: the gate is direct but heavily guarded, the shaft is stealthy but physically challenging, and the lava tube is unguarded but dangerously hot. Let the party debate and plan — this is their heist-planning moment.
loot: Brunda's hand-drawn map of Ironslag (provides advantage on Navigation checks inside the complex)
Intelligence on guard rotations (provides one free group Stealth success inside Ironslag before needing to roll)
Knowledge of the control rod's location and function (critical quest information)
The gratitude of 12 freed captives (story reward — word of the party's heroism will spread)

acts.title: Act 2: The Adamantine Forge
acts.description: The party infiltrates Ironslag proper, navigating the outer forges and penetrating to the central Adamantine Forge where the Vonindod stands in terrifying near-completion. The environment is the primary enemy in this act — extreme heat, molten metal, deafening noise, and the constant presence of fire giant patrols create a hostile landscape where every moment tests the party's endurance and resourcefulness. The enslaved workers present opportunities for aid and intelligence, the azers can be freed to provide fire-immune allies, and the forge machinery itself can be sabotaged to create diversions. The act culminates in the party reaching the Adamantine Forge and confronting Duchess Brimskarda, who oversees the Vonindod's final assembly with a perfectionism that matches her husband's ambition.
objectives: Infiltrate Ironslag through the chosen entry point (main gate, ventilation shaft, or lava tube)
Navigate the outer forges while avoiding or defeating fire giant patrols
Free the enslaved azers by destroying their binding braziers (optional but provides powerful allies)
Reach the Adamantine Forge and witness the Vonindod's scale and near-completion
Confront or bypass Duchess Brimskarda to access Duke Zalto's war room above

scenes.name: Into the Furnace
scenes.description: The party enters Ironslag through their chosen route and navigates the outer forges — a hellish industrial complex of blast furnaces, smelting chambers, and slave barracks. The heat is severe, the noise deafening, and the ever-present threat of fire giant patrols creates constant tension. The party can choose stealth, sabotage, or direct action, with each approach offering different advantages and risks.
scenes.readAloud: "The heat hits you like a physical force as you cross the threshold into Ironslag. It is not the dry heat of a desert or the humid heat of a jungle — it is the focused, aggressive heat of a furnace, pressing against your skin with malicious intent, sucking the moisture from your eyes and turning every breath into an effort. The outer forges stretch before you in a vast cavern whose ceiling is lost in smoke and steam, lit by the hellish orange glow of blast furnaces the size of houses. Rivers of molten metal flow through carved channels in the floor, their surfaces rippling with slow, hypnotic menace, and the air above them shimmers with thermal distortion that makes the far walls dance and blur. The noise is staggering — a wall of sound composed of hammers striking metal, bellows wheezing, chains rattling, and the deep, constant rumble of the volcano itself. Shapes move through the haze: fire giants, their coal-black skin gleaming with sweat and reflected forge-light, striding between the furnaces with casual ownership. Smaller shapes scurry at their feet — the enslaved workers, dwarves and humans moving in shuffling lines from furnace to forge to smelter, their skin angry red from the heat, their movements mechanical and hopeless. Hell hounds pace the perimeter, their red eyes scanning for anything out of place. And everywhere, the product of this misery: stacked ingots of adamantine, iron beams shaped for the Vonindod's skeleton, and barrel-sized rivets destined for the joints of a colossus. The industry of destruction, operating at full capacity, never pausing, never stopping, consuming lives to build a weapon that will consume civilizations."

skillChecks.success: The deafening noise of the forges masks your movements. You navigate through the outer forges by timing your movement to the rhythm of the hammers and using the steam and smoke for concealment. The fire giant patrols pass within feet of your hiding spots without noticing.
skillChecks.failure: A hell hound catches your scent and begins tracking the party. The group has 3 rounds to relocate or silence the hound before it alerts a fire giant patrol.

skillChecks.success: You endure the extreme heat without faltering, maintaining your focus and physical capability despite conditions that would incapacitate most surface-dwellers.
skillChecks.failure: The heat is overwhelming. You gain 1 level of exhaustion from the thermal stress, and sweat stings your eyes — disadvantage on Perception checks for the next hour.

skillChecks.success: You identify the binding braziers that enslave the azers — ornate brass censers mounted on the forge walls, each one connected to a group of fire elementals by threads of binding magic visible only to those attuned to the arcane. There are three braziers in the outer forges. Destroying all three would free a dozen azers — powerful fire-immune allies in this environment.
skillChecks.failure: The azers are clearly not working willingly — their movements are jerky and reluctant, and they flinch whenever they approach certain objects on the walls. But the mechanism of their enslavement is not immediately apparent.

combatEncounters.tactics: If the party is detected, the fire giant overseers attack with coordinated brutality. One engages in melee while the other throws rocks from range, targeting spellcasters. The hell hounds use fire breath on clustered party members, then engage whoever is closest to the slave barracks — the giants value their workforce and want to prevent the party from freeing slaves during combat. The overseers will attempt to push party members toward molten metal channels (Shove action, contested Athletics vs. DC 20). If one giant falls, the other sounds an alarm horn that brings 2 more hell hounds from adjacent chambers within 3 rounds.
combatEncounters.terrain: Outer forge chamber (120 ft by 80 ft). 4 blast furnaces (15 ft tall, full cover) positioned in a grid pattern. Molten metal channels (5 ft wide) divide the room into quadrants — crossing requires DC 12 Acrobatics or 3d6 fire damage on failure. Slave barracks entrance on the east wall (narrow passage, medium creatures only). Forge equipment provides half cover throughout. Ambient noise grants advantage on Stealth but disadvantage on hearing-based Perception.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The outer forges should feel like descending into an industrialized hell. The horror here is not supernatural — it is the mundane horror of slavery, industrial exploitation, and the dehumanization of captive laborers. The enslaved workers do not look up when the party passes because hope has been beaten out of them. The fire giants do not treat their slaves with particular cruelty — to them, the captives are tools, no different from the hammers and tongs. That casual indifference is more disturbing than outright sadism. If the party frees azers, play the moment as genuinely moving — these elemental beings have been enslaved against their nature, forced to work in service of their captors. Their gratitude is fierce and immediate, expressed through flares of purifying flame and a readiness to fight that borders on recklessness. The binding braziers are opportunities for the party to gain powerful allies, but each one destroyed creates noise and smoke that might alert patrols.
loot: Confiscated adventurer gear from a hidden alcove: cloak of fire resistance (uncommon, requires attunement), 2 potions of fire resistance, adventurer's pack with 50 gp in mixed coins
Map of the inner forge marked with guard positions (found with the confiscated gear — provides advantage on navigation in the Adamantine Forge)
Binding brazier components (if destroyed — worth 75 gp each for the enchanted brass, 225 gp total)
Hell hound teeth and fire giant weapons (200 gp total salvage value)

scenes.name: The Iron Colossus
scenes.description: The party reaches the Adamantine Forge — the central cathedral-scale chamber where the Vonindod stands in terrifying near-completion. This is the first time the party sees the colossus up close, and its sheer scale should be overwhelming. Duchess Brimskarda oversees the final assembly operations from a platform at the 60-foot level, and the chamber is patrolled by fire giant smiths and their salamander assistants. The party must navigate the chamber, deal with Brimskarda, and find access to Duke Zalto's war room above.
scenes.readAloud: "The passage from the outer forges opens onto a ledge, and the world falls away beneath you. The Adamantine Forge is not a room — it is a cathedral hollowed out of the mountain's volcanic heart, a vertical oval of dark stone three hundred feet from floor to vaulted ceiling, lit from below by rivers of molten rock that flow through carved channels like luminous veins in the body of the earth. The heat is a physical assault, and the air shimmers with distortion that makes the far walls ripple like water. But you barely notice any of it. Because standing in the center of the chamber, mounted on a scaffold of iron beams and surrounded by work platforms at thirty, sixty, and ninety feet, is the Vonindod. And it is beyond anything you imagined. The colossus stands nearly a hundred feet tall — a humanoid figure of dark adamantine and enchanted iron, every plate and joint fitted with a precision that speaks of genius twisted to terrible purpose. Its legs are pillars thick enough to support a castle. Its arms end in fists the size of wagons. Its torso is a fortress, armored in overlapping plates of adamantine that gleam with a dark, oily sheen in the forge-light. And its head — an iron skull crowned with a helm of swept-back horns — stares down at you with eyes of dark ruby, empty and waiting. The chest cavity is open, a gaping wound in the construct's torso that exposes a hollow chamber where something — the control rod, you realize — must be inserted to give this monstrosity life. Even inert, the Vonindod radiates a presence that makes your skin crawl. This is not a weapon. This is an extinction event waiting to happen. On the sixty-foot platform, silhouetted against the colossus's chest, a fire giant woman in ornate armor directs a team of salamanders with sharp, precise gestures. Duchess Brimskarda. She has not seen you yet, but her hell hound companion raises its head from the platform and sniffs the air with sudden interest."

skillChecks.success: You study the Vonindod's construction and identify several vulnerabilities: the four conduit pipes connecting the colossus to Maegera's prison below are the primary power supply — severing them would drain the construct of elemental energy. The scaffold itself has structural weak points that could be exploited to collapse sections of the work platform. And the control rod socket in the chest cavity shows signs of modification from the original ancient design — Zalto has adapted it for his own use, and the adaptation introduces a potential feedback vulnerability.
skillChecks.failure: The Vonindod is enormous and terrifying, but its specific construction details are difficult to analyze from a distance. You would need to get closer — much closer — to identify exploitable weaknesses.

skillChecks.success: You navigate the chamber's lower level using the scaffold supports and work equipment for cover, avoiding the patrol routes of the fire giant smiths and their salamander assistants. The ambient noise and heat distortion work in your favor.
skillChecks.failure: A salamander working on the Vonindod's leg joint spots you and hisses an alarm in Ignan. Brimskarda looks down from her platform, and her expression shifts from concentration to predatory interest. Combat is imminent.

skillChecks.success: If combat with Brimskarda has not yet begun, you may attempt to parley. Brimskarda is more pragmatic than her husband — she can be convinced that the Vonindod project is doomed if you present evidence of the party's strength and the instability of Zalto's alliance with Surtur. She will not betray Zalto, but she may step aside temporarily if she believes doing so serves her own survival.
skillChecks.failure: Brimskarda is unimpressed. 'You have come to the heart of fire giant power and you think words will save you? You are fuel. Nothing more.' Combat begins.

enemies: Duchess Brimskarda (CR 9 fire giant with spellcasting: fireball 3/day, heat metal at will, wall of fire 1/day)
combatEncounters.tactics: Brimskarda fights from the 60-ft platform, using wall of fire to divide the battlefield and fireball to target clustered enemies below. She uses heat metal on any party member wearing heavy armor — the DC 14 Constitution save to avoid dropping the equipment becomes crucial in a fight where fire damage is already constant. The fire giant smiths engage in melee on the ground level, using the forge equipment as improvised weapons (hammers that deal an additional 1d6 fire damage from residual heat). The salamanders use their heated body trait to punish melee attackers (2d6 fire damage on hit or when touched) and their spear attacks from flanking positions. The magma mephits erupt from the molten rivers at the start of round 2 and attack the nearest non-fire-giant creatures with fire breath (15-ft cone, DC 11 Dex save, 2d6 fire damage). Brimskarda will retreat toward the war room staircase if reduced below 40 HP, attempting to warn Zalto. Preventing her escape is critical to maintaining surprise for Act 3.
combatEncounters.terrain: Adamantine Forge chamber (200 ft by 150 ft, 300 ft ceiling). The Vonindod stands at the center on its scaffold. Work platforms at 30, 60, and 90 ft connected by ladders and walkways. Molten rock rivers (5-15 ft wide) divide the ground level — 6d10 fire damage per round to any creature in the lava, no save. Iron bridges (5-10 ft wide) span the channels. Some bridges are heat-stressed (DC 13 Investigation to identify) and collapse under 500+ lbs. The Vonindod itself can be climbed (DC 14 Athletics) and its surface is warm but not damaging. The 60-ft platform is 20 ft by 30 ft with a railing. The staircase to the war room is at the chamber's north end, 90 ft up.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The reveal of the Vonindod should be one of the most dramatic moments in the campaign. This is the first time the party sees the physical manifestation of Zalto's ambition, and it should be awe-inspiring and terrifying in equal measure. Take time with the description — let the scale sink in. A hundred-foot colossus is taller than most buildings the party has ever seen, and it is made of adamantine, the hardest metal in existence. The Vonindod is not just a construct — it is a statement of intent, a declaration that fire giants will reshape the world by force. Brimskarda is a worthy adversary in her own right — she is Zalto's equal in intelligence if not in raw ambition, and she runs the forge operations with an efficiency that has made the Vonindod's near-completion possible. She is not blindly loyal to Zalto but deeply invested in the project as a work of engineering genius. If the party can appeal to her pride as a craftsperson rather than threatening her as an enemy, she may be more amenable to negotiation. The salamanders are enslaved through magical coercion and fight reluctantly — if the binding is somehow disrupted, they will flee rather than continue fighting.
loot: Duchess Brimskarda's enchanted warhammer (+1, deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on hit)
Brimskarda's signet ring (grants access to locked chambers in the war room level)
Salamander spears (4, each deals an additional 1d6 fire damage — the enchantment fades in 24 hours once removed from Ironslag's heat)
Forge master's tools (masterwork artisan's tools worth 200 gp, advantage on smithing-related checks)
150 gp in fire giant currency (heavy iron coins stamped with Zalto's seal)

acts.title: Act 3: The Iron Duke
acts.description: The climax of the scenario. The party ascends to Duke Zalto's war room to confront the fire giant lord and seize or destroy the control rod. Zalto is the most dangerous individual opponent the party has faced — a fire giant of exceptional strength and tactical acumen, enhanced by legendary actions and driven by an ambition that borders on religious fervor. Multiple paths to victory exist: direct combat against Zalto, destruction of the control rod, sabotage of the Vonindod from within, or the desperate gambit of descending to Maegera's prison and freeing or partially releasing the fire primordial. Each path has different consequences and costs, and the party's choices will have repercussions that echo through the remainder of the campaign. The third conch shell of teleportation is found here, bringing the party one step closer to the Maelstrom and the final confrontation.
objectives: Reach Duke Zalto's war room and confront the Iron Duke
Acquire or destroy the control rod to prevent the Vonindod's activation
Obtain the third conch shell of teleportation
Decide the fate of Ironslag: targeted destruction, total annihilation (freeing Maegera), or surgical neutralization
Escape Ironslag with the conch shell and any freed captives

scenes.name: The War Room
scenes.description: The party enters Duke Zalto's war room — a chamber of polished obsidian filled with war plans, trophies, and the enchanted relief map of the Sword Coast that reveals the full scope of Zalto's planned conquest. The control rod rests in its holder beside Zalto's iron throne. Zalto himself may or may not be present depending on whether the alarm has been raised — if the party has been stealthy, Zalto is in his private chambers and can be ambushed; if the alarm is active, he is waiting with his honor guard.
scenes.readAloud: "The staircase from the forge chamber spirals upward through rock that grows cooler with every step — a relief so profound it feels like stepping into winter after hours in a furnace. The passage opens into a chamber that would be impressive in any fortress but here, above the volcanic chaos below, feels almost civilized. Almost. The war room is carved from polished obsidian that reflects the firelight from iron sconces in dark, distorted mirrors. Weapon racks line the walls, holding greatswords large enough to cleave a horse in two. Trophy cases display the broken armaments of those who challenged Duke Zalto and lost — you see a paladin's holy symbol, snapped in half; a dragon's fang, mounted on a plaque; shields bearing the heraldry of kingdoms you recognize, their surfaces dented and scorched. At the room's center stands the war table: a three-dimensional relief map of the Sword Coast carved from volcanic stone, ten feet across, enchanted with illusions that show tiny figures moving in formation — fire giant battalions, siege trains, and at the head of them all, a miniature Vonindod striding through a miniature Waterdeep, crushing miniature buildings beneath its iron feet. The detail is extraordinary. Zalto has planned the destruction of civilization with the precision of a master strategist. And there, beside a throne of iron that glows dull red from the magma channel heating it from below, rests the control rod — a six-foot shaft of adamantine, inscribed with runes that pulse with a contained elemental fury. It hums. Even from across the room, you can feel its power: the bridge between a giant's will and a colossus's body. In the wrong hands, it is the key to an apocalypse. A second object sits on a shelf behind the throne: a conch shell, large enough to hold in two hands, carved from something that is not quite shell and not quite stone. It radiates a faint, cold magic utterly unlike the fire that dominates this place. The third conch shell."

skillChecks.success: You study Zalto's war table and grasp the full scope of his ambition. The invasion plans are detailed and terrifyingly competent: a systematic conquest of the Sword Coast, starting with the mining settlements and working toward the major cities. Timetables, supply lines, garrison requirements — Zalto has thought of everything. More importantly, you notice that the plans assume Surtur's blessing, but there is no evidence that Surtur has actually sanctioned the campaign. The war table shows Zalto's vision, not divine mandate. This could be a lever in negotiation.
skillChecks.failure: The war table shows invasion plans for the Sword Coast, but the strategic details are too complex to analyze quickly under pressure.

skillChecks.success: You remove the control rod from its holder without triggering the fire trap — a careful manipulation of the rod's weight and the holder's pressure mechanism.
skillChecks.failure: The holder's fire trap triggers as you lift the rod: 4d6 fire damage (DC 14 Dexterity save for half) and a blast of flame that illuminates the room and alerts anyone within earshot.

skillChecks.success: You study the control rod and understand its function completely. It is both a command interface and a power conduit — when inserted into the Vonindod's chest cavity, it channels Maegera's elemental energy through the operator and into the construct. Destroying the rod would render the Vonindod permanently inert. But you also realize it could be used as a weapon: the concentrated elemental energy within could be released in a single devastating burst if the rod's containment runes are disrupted — essentially a bomb that deals 10d6 fire damage in a 40-ft radius (DC 16 Dex save for half).
skillChecks.failure: The control rod is clearly magical and important, but its specific function and capabilities are unclear beyond its obvious connection to the Vonindod.

skillChecks.success: You find the hidden passage behind Zalto's throne — a narrow corridor that descends sharply into increasing heat. This is Zalto's private route to Maegera's prison. It is unguarded because Zalto never expected anyone to find it.
skillChecks.failure: The war room appears to have only the single entrance from the forge staircase. The hidden passage remains concealed.

scenes.roleplayNotes: If the party reaches the war room without raising the alarm, this scene is about exploration, intelligence gathering, and the decision of what to do with the control rod. The war table is a treasure trove of strategic information that would be invaluable to the Lords' Alliance, the Harpers, or any other faction opposing the giant war. The trophy cases tell a story of Zalto's previous victories — each broken weapon represents someone who tried and failed to stop him. The conch shell is the party's ticket to the Maelstrom, but they must first deal with Zalto and the Vonindod. If the alarm has been raised, Zalto is here waiting, and this scene merges directly with the next one. The control rod presents a compelling choice: keep it (and risk it falling into the wrong hands), destroy it (permanently disabling the Vonindod), or weaponize it (a powerful but one-use option). Let the party debate — this decision has real consequences.
loot: The control rod of the Vonindod (artifact-level quest item — can be destroyed, weaponized, or kept)
Third Conch of Teleportation (teleports the party to the Maelstrom)
Zalto's war plans (strategic intelligence worth significant political capital with surface factions)
Trophy case equipment: +1 shield, +1 longsword, 3 potions of fire resistance
Sending stone paired with Countess Sansuri (intelligence about cloud giant politics)
120 gp in Zalto's personal strongbox

scenes.name: The Iron Duke
scenes.description: The confrontation with Duke Zalto — the most dangerous single opponent the party has faced. Zalto is a fire giant of exceptional power, enhanced by his connection to Maegera and driven by an ambition that has consumed his entire existence. The fight can begin in the war room, the forge chamber, or Maegera's prison depending on how events unfold, and Zalto's tactics shift depending on the location and context. Multiple resolution paths exist: direct combat, negotiation through the revelation that Surtur has not sanctioned his plans, or the nuclear option of freeing Maegera.
scenes.readAloud: "Duke Zalto fills the doorway like a wall of dark iron and burning ambition. He is larger than any fire giant you have encountered — eighteen feet of muscle and rage, his coal-black skin webbed with glowing cracks like cooling magma, his eyes twin furnaces of orange-white intensity. He wears armor forged from the same adamantine as the Vonindod, and it fits him like a second skin — articulated plates that gleam with dark menace and radiate heat intense enough to blur the air around him. In his right hand he carries a greatsword that could split an ox from crown to tail, its blade inscribed with runes that glow the same orange-white as his eyes. His left hand is a fist the size of an anvil. He does not rush. He does not roar. He enters the room with the measured, deliberate pace of someone who has never met an opponent worth rushing for, and his gaze sweeps across the party with the evaluating precision of a master smith assessing raw materials. When he speaks, his voice is the deep, resonant boom of a forge hammer striking adamantine — controlled, powerful, and utterly certain. 'You have killed my wife's servants. You have freed my workers. You have touched my rod.' The last word comes out like a sentence of death. 'I am Zalto, Duke of Ironslag, Lord of the Adamantine Forge, Builder of the Vonindod. And you —' he lifts the greatsword to point directly at the party, the blade's heat making the air between them shimmer — 'are the last interruption I will ever suffer. When the Vonindod walks, the world will kneel. And your bones will be among the foundations.'"

skillChecks.success: You present evidence that Surtur has not sanctioned Zalto's plans for the Vonindod — that Zalto's bid for Ordning supremacy is built on assumption, not divine mandate. The blow to Zalto's certainty is visible: a flicker of doubt crosses his face, his grip on the greatsword loosens fractionally. He does not surrender, but his legendary resistances are reduced by 1 and his attacks lose the certainty that made them devastating — he suffers disadvantage on his first attack roll each round for the remainder of the fight.
skillChecks.failure: Zalto laughs — a sound like a furnace bellowing. 'Surtur speaks through fire and conquest. I AM his mandate.' The attempt to shake his confidence fails, and his certainty in his divine right only hardens.

skillChecks.success: You invoke the ancient fire giant codes — the laws of the forge that even a Duke must respect. A formal challenge, fire-to-fire, gives the party the right to single combat against Zalto's champion. If the party's champion wins, Zalto must concede the control rod. This is not a trick — fire giants take forge-law seriously. Zalto will honor the terms... but he will choose himself as his champion.
skillChecks.failure: Your attempt to invoke fire giant tradition falls flat — either the wrong words, the wrong context, or Zalto simply does not care about formalities when his life's work is threatened.

skillChecks.success: You describe what the party has already accomplished — the other giant lords defeated, the alliances broken, the forces that are already converging on the fire giant position. Zalto is not intimidated, but he recognizes the tactical reality: the party is dangerous, and fighting them costs time and resources he cannot afford. He may offer a deal — the conch shell for the party's withdrawal, leaving the Vonindod intact. It is a devil's bargain.
skillChecks.failure: Zalto is unimpressed. 'Others have come with threats. Their weapons decorate my walls.' He gestures at the trophy cases.

enemies: Duke Zalto (CR 12 fire giant with legendary actions — see below)
combatEncounters.tactics: DUKE ZALTO — Modified Fire Giant (CR 12): HP 200, AC 18 (adamantine plate), Speed 40 ft. STR 25 (+7), DEX 9 (-1), CON 23 (+6), INT 14 (+2), WIS 14 (+2), CHA 16 (+3). Saves: STR +12, CON +11, CHA +8. Damage Immunities: fire. Skills: Athletics +12, Intimidation +8, Perception +7. ATTACKS: Multiattack (2 greatsword or 2 rocks). Adamantine Greatsword: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft, 6d6+7 slashing plus 2d6 fire damage. Rock: +12 to hit, range 60/240, 4d10+7 bludgeoning. LEGENDARY ACTIONS (3/round): Greatsword Strike (1 action), Commanding Presence (1 action — one allied fire giant within 60 ft makes a free attack), Volcanic Stomp (2 actions — all creatures within 15 ft make DC 17 STR save or are knocked prone and take 2d8 bludgeoning). LEGENDARY RESISTANCES: 3/day. SPECIAL: Forge Lord's Fury — when Zalto drops below 100 HP, his eyes blaze white-hot. He gains +2 to hit and +1d6 fire damage on all attacks for the remainder of the combat. The honor guards fight in coordinated formation with Zalto, flanking targets and using Shove actions to push party members toward the war table (which Zalto will smash through a target for 2d6 bludgeoning) or toward the staircase leading down to the forge. If one honor guard falls, the other fights more desperately, gaining advantage on attacks but losing its defensive coordination (AC reduced by 2).
combatEncounters.terrain: War room (60 ft by 40 ft). Zalto's iron throne at the north end. War table at the center (provides half cover but can be destroyed — AC 15, 30 HP). Trophy cases along the walls (can be smashed for improvised weapons or to scatter debris — difficult terrain in 10-ft radius). The staircase down to the forge at the south end — if combat spills down the stairs, it moves to the Adamantine Forge terrain. The obsidian walls reflect firelight and can create confusing reflections (DC 12 Perception to avoid being surprised by attacks from unexpected angles). The hidden passage behind the throne (if discovered) leads to Maegera's prison — a potential escape route or the path to the nuclear option.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Zalto should be the most memorable villain of the campaign so far. He is not a mindless brute — he is a visionary, a strategist, and a true believer in fire giant supremacy. He has spent decades on the Vonindod project, enslaved thousands, and killed anyone who stood in his way, all in service of a dream he considers divine. His confidence is earned — he has never lost a fight, never had his plans derailed, and never doubted that fire would prove the strongest element in the new Ordning. The party is the first real threat to that certainty, and how Zalto responds depends on how the party approaches him. If they come with force, he meets force with force — he is a fire giant duke, and he was born for this. If they come with words, he listens with the contemptuous patience of someone humoring children. If they come with evidence that undermines his divine mandate, he is shaken — not broken, but shaken, and that crack in his armor is the party's best weapon. Play his legendary actions aggressively — Volcanic Stomp to control the battlefield, Commanding Presence to coordinate with his guards, and Greatsword Strike to punish anyone who turns their back. Forge Lord's Fury should feel like a desperate escalation, not a power-up — Zalto is losing for the first time in his life, and his response is to burn brighter.
