Dwarven Plate armor (very rare, requires attunement — recovered from Zalto's trophy collection, originally belonging to a dwarf king who challenged the fire giants centuries ago; AC 20, advantage on saving throws against being forcibly moved)
Zalto's adamantine plate armor (fire giant sized — worth 500 gp as raw adamantine if dismantled)
250 gp in Zalto's personal treasury

scenes.name: The Nuclear Option
scenes.description: If the party chooses to descend to Maegera's prison — either as a desperate gambit during the fight with Zalto, a calculated strategy to destroy the Vonindod permanently, or an act of mercy to free the imprisoned primordial — this scene covers the consequences. Freeing Maegera is the most dramatic and consequential action available in the scenario, triggering a volcanic eruption that destroys Ironslag, the Vonindod, and everything within the complex. The party has a limited number of rounds to escape before the mountain comes down.
scenes.readAloud: "The hidden passage behind Zalto's throne descends steeply, the temperature rising with every step until the walls themselves glow cherry-red and the air becomes a physical weight of heat pressing against your lungs. The passage opens into a spherical chamber that takes your breath away — not from the heat, though the heat is terrible, but from what you see. At the chamber's center, suspended by six chains of adamantine thicker than your body, Maegera burns. The fire primordial is not a creature you can comprehend — it is a living sun, a sentient conflagration compressed into a space the size of a house, its flames cycling through colors you have never seen, radiating a fury so intense it makes your bones vibrate. The binding runes on the adamantine walls glow cold blue — the only cold thing in this volcanic hell — and the chains hum with a tension that speaks of millennia of captive rage. A control platform near the entrance bristles with levers and rune-inscribed wheels, the mechanisms by which the ancient fire giants regulate the primordial's power output. Conduit pipes — four of them, each as thick as a tree trunk — extend from the chamber walls upward toward the forges and the Vonindod above. Through them, Maegera's stolen energy flows, powering everything in Ironslag. And Maegera itself... you cannot hear it, not with your ears, but you feel it — a pulse of emotion so raw and vast it bypasses thought entirely. Rage. Grief. A loneliness measured in centuries. And beneath it all, a desperate, wordless plea: free me. Free me. Free me."

skillChecks.success: You understand the binding mechanism completely. A full release — severing all six chains and disrupting the binding runes — would free Maegera entirely, causing an immediate volcanic eruption that destroys everything within a mile radius and devastates the surrounding region for weeks. A partial release — opening the binding just enough to send a power surge through the conduit pipes — would overload and destroy the Vonindod without fully freeing Maegera. The partial option requires precise manipulation of the control platform: DC 18 Arcana to execute.
skillChecks.failure: The binding is clearly ancient and powerful, but the specifics of how to manipulate it safely are beyond your current understanding. You can see the chains and the control platform, but operating the mechanism is trial and error — and error here could be catastrophic.

skillChecks.success: You connect with Maegera's emotional projection and understand the primordial's desires: freedom above all, vengeance against the fire giants who imprisoned it, and a return to the elemental plane of fire. Maegera is not evil — it is an elemental force, as amoral as a wildfire. It will not deliberately target the party if freed, but it will not protect them either. The eruption will be indiscriminate.
skillChecks.failure: Maegera's emotional projection is overwhelming — rage and pain and loneliness blur together into a psychic noise that makes concentration difficult. The primordial's specific desires are unclear.

skillChecks.success: You physically sever one of the adamantine chains using sustained effort and whatever tools are available. Each chain severed weakens the binding — at three chains, Maegera begins to break free on its own, giving the party 10 rounds to escape before full release.
skillChecks.failure: The adamantine chains are incredibly resilient. Your attempt fails and the backlash of elemental energy deals 2d6 fire damage.

combatEncounters.tactics: The chamber's wardens fight to protect the binding — they are conditioned to prevent any interference with Maegera's prison. The salamanders attack whoever approaches the control platform or the chains, using their heated body to punish melee attacks. The magma mephits swarm spellcasters to disrupt concentration. If Zalto is still alive and aware of what the party is doing, he arrives in 5 rounds, roaring with fury — this is his ultimate line in the sand, and he fights with Forge Lord's Fury active from the start.
combatEncounters.terrain: Spherical chamber (300 ft diameter). Maegera at the center (approach within 30 ft requires DC 17 Constitution save or 2d6 fire damage per round). Control platform near the entrance (15 ft by 10 ft). 6 adamantine chains extending from the walls to Maegera (AC 20, 50 HP each, immune to fire). 4 conduit pipes along the walls (AC 16, 30 HP each). The heat is extreme throughout — DC 15 Constitution saves every round or take 1d6 fire damage (fire resistance reduces to DC 12, immunity negates).

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene should feel like the party is standing at the edge of a decision with world-shaking consequences. Freeing Maegera is not simply pulling a lever — it is an act that will reshape the geography of the region and potentially kill thousands. The partial release option (overloading the Vonindod without fully freeing the primordial) is the surgically precise alternative, but it requires high skill checks and leaves Maegera still imprisoned — a moral compromise that some characters may struggle with. If Zalto arrives during this scene, the emotional intensity is maximum — he will fight with everything he has to prevent the party from touching his life's work, his power source, and his claim to Ordning supremacy. The decision to free or partially free Maegera should be a party decision, not a single character's choice — give everyone a moment to weigh in before the final action is taken.
loot: Maegera's Ember (very rare, requires attunement — a crystallized fragment of the fire primordial's essence, shed during the partial or full release. Functions as a fire elemental gem that can summon a fire elemental 1/day, and grants the attuned wielder resistance to fire damage and the ability to cast fireball once per long rest at 5th level)
Adamantine chain links (if chains are severed — each link is worth 100 gp as raw adamantine, 6 links recoverable if the party has time)

scenes.name: Escape from Ironslag
scenes.description: With the Vonindod neutralized, the control rod acquired or destroyed, and Zalto defeated or dead, the party must escape Ironslag. If Maegera was fully freed, this is a desperate race against a volcanic eruption. If the Vonindod was sabotaged without freeing the primordial, the escape is less frantic but still dangerous as the forge complex reacts to the destruction. The third conch shell provides an emergency exit — but using it teleports the party directly to the Maelstrom, and any freed captives left behind will need to find their own way out.
scenes.readAloud: "The mountain screams. Whether you freed Maegera, sabotaged the Vonindod, or simply killed the tyrant who built it, Ironslag knows something fundamental has changed. The walls tremble. Cracks spider through the obsidian. In the forge below, the Vonindod — that monument to conquest and cruelty — stands dark and lifeless, its chest cavity empty, its ruby eyes dimming as the elemental power drains away. It will never walk. It will never crush a city. It will never kneel a world. But the mountain does not care about victory or symbolism. The mountain cares about geology, and the geology is angry. Lava surges through channels that were never designed for this volume. Steam erupts from every vent and fissure. The sound is beyond thunder — it is the voice of the earth itself, protesting the violation of its depths. You have what you came for: the conch shell, cold and strange in your hand, humming with a power that could carry you to safety in an instant. But behind you, in the tunnels and barracks and slave quarters of Ironslag, people are still chained. People you came here to save. The mountain gives you a choice, and it gives you very little time to make it."

skillChecks.success: The party navigates the collapsing tunnels at speed, dodging falling debris, leaping across widening cracks, and pushing through steam vents that were not there moments ago. Everyone makes it to the exit — or to a point where the conch shell can be safely activated.
skillChecks.failure: The collapsing tunnels are treacherous. Each character who fails takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage from falling rock and debris, and the group's pace is slowed — reducing the escape window by 2 rounds.

skillChecks.success: You rally the enslaved workers, breaking through their shock and hopelessness with urgent commands and reassurance. The freed azers (if available) help guide the slaves through passages they know well. Most of the captives escape.
skillChecks.failure: The enslaved workers are too shocked and confused to respond quickly. Some follow the party, but others scatter in panic. Without firm guidance, many will be lost in the collapsing tunnels.

skillChecks.success: You identify the safest route through the collapsing complex — avoiding areas where lava flows are increasing, selecting tunnels with the most structural integrity, and timing your movement between tremors. The escape is harrowing but controlled.
skillChecks.failure: The route is chosen poorly — the party encounters a section of tunnel where the floor has given way to a lava channel. A detour costs 2 rounds and forces additional Constitution saves against heat (DC 14, 2d6 fire damage on failure).

enemies: Collapsing environment — not a traditional combat encounter
combatEncounters.tactics: This is a skill challenge rather than a traditional fight. Each round, the environment attacks: falling rocks (DC 13 Dex save, 2d6 bludgeoning on failure), steam eruptions (DC 12 Con save, 1d6 fire damage on failure), and widening cracks that require DC 12 Athletics to leap across. If Maegera was fully freed, the intensity doubles after round 5: DCs increase by 2 and damage dice increase by one step. The party has 10 rounds to escape before the tunnel systems become impassable. The conch shell can be used at any time as an emergency exit, but it only teleports the party — no captives can come along unless they are physically touching a party member.
combatEncounters.terrain: Collapsing Ironslag tunnel system. Variable width (10-20 ft). Falling debris creates difficult terrain that shifts each round. Lava breaks through the floor in random locations (10 ft by 10 ft, 6d10 fire damage). Steam vents reduce visibility to 10 ft in affected areas. Emergency exit points: the main gate (if still standing), the ventilation shaft, or the lava tube entrance — each has its own hazards in the collapse.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The escape from Ironslag should be cinematic and intense — a reward for the party's victory, not a punishment. The mountain is collapsing, but the party has already won. The tension here is moral rather than physical: do they use the conch shell and escape instantly, or do they spend precious rounds freeing captives and guiding them to safety? There is no wrong answer, but the choice should have weight. If the azers were freed earlier, they are invaluable here — immune to the fire and familiar with the tunnels, they can guide groups of captives to safety while the party focuses on their own escape. The final moments of the escape should feel triumphant: emerging from the mountain into cold mountain air, looking back to see Ironslag's furnace-glow dimming for the first time in decades, knowing that the Vonindod will never walk and Zalto's dream of fire giant supremacy has been extinguished. Then the conch shell hums in the party's hand, and the next chapter — the Maelstrom — awaits.
loot: Third Conch of Teleportation (if not already acquired — found on Zalto's body or in the war room)
Gratitude of freed captives (story reward — reputation with surface factions significantly improved)

If azers were freed: a gift of elemental gratitude — one party member may receive a permanent minor blessing: +1 to fire damage rolls or resistance to cold damage (azer's choice based on what they observed in combat)

npcsInvolved.name: Duke Zalto
npcsInvolved.description: An eighteen-foot fire giant of exceptional power and intelligence, clad in adamantine plate armor that glows with residual forge-heat. His skin is coal-black webbed with glowing cracks like cooling magma, and his eyes burn with the orange-white intensity of a blast furnace at full capacity. He carries an adamantine greatsword inscribed with runes of fire and conquest.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Zalto is a true believer in fire giant supremacy. He has spent decades assembling the Vonindod because he genuinely believes that fire — industry, warfare, the forge — is the strongest element and that fire giants should rule the new Ordning. He plans to present the activated Vonindod to Surtur as proof of his devotion and worthiness. His ambition is religious in its intensity and leaves no room for doubt or compromise.

npcsInvolved.name: Duchess Brimskarda
npcsInvolved.description: Zalto's wife and the operational commander of Ironslag's forge operations. She is slightly shorter than Zalto but more refined in bearing, with an engineer's precision in her movements and a strategist's calculation in her eyes. She wears enchanted armor and carries a warhammer that pulses with fire magic.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Brimskarda is invested in the Vonindod as a work of engineering genius rather than a divine mandate. She respects the craft more than the ideology, which makes her marginally more pragmatic than her husband. She can be negotiated with — barely — if the party can appeal to her survival instincts or her pride as a master smith. She will not openly betray Zalto, but she may choose discretion over valor if the situation is clearly lost.

npcsInvolved.name: Brunda Ironmantle
npcsInvolved.description: A broad-shouldered dwarven master smith with a branded cheek and hands scarred by forge work. Her eyes burn with a defiance that months of slavery could not extinguish. She speaks with the precise, measured cadence of a craftsperson describing a technical problem — even when the problem is the destruction of a world-ending weapon.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Brunda was enslaved after Zalto's forces raided her hold. She was kept alive because her metalworking skills were too valuable to waste, and she was forced to work on the Vonindod's most delicate components. She has been memorizing every detail of the construct and the forge complex, planning for the day someone came to destroy it. Her motivation is revenge channeled through usefulness — she wants Ironslag destroyed, and she will do everything in her power to help the party accomplish that.

npcsInvolved.name: Maegera the Dawn Titan
npcsInvolved.description: A fire primordial — not a creature in any conventional sense but a living conflagration, a sentient sun compressed to the size of a house and chained with adamantine for over a thousand years. Maegera communicates through emotion rather than language: rage, grief, loneliness, and an overwhelming desire for freedom.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Freedom. Maegera wants to be released from its millennial imprisonment and return to the elemental plane of fire. It does not hate the party or love the party — it is an elemental force, as amoral as a wildfire. If freed, it will destroy everything in its path not out of malice but because that is its nature. The party must decide whether Maegera's suffering justifies the collateral damage of its release.

dmTips: The heat should be a constant, oppressive presence throughout the scenario — not just a mechanical hazard but a narrative tool. Describe sweat evaporating, metal becoming painful to touch, leather drying and cracking, breath feeling like inhaling from an oven. The party should never forget they are inside a volcano, and the relief of cooler areas should feel like a reward.

The Vonindod reveal should be one of the campaign's defining moments. Take your time with the description. A hundred-foot colossus of adamantine is beyond anything the party has ever seen — let them feel the scale, the craftsmanship, and the terror of what it would mean if this thing walked. Comparisons to buildings, ships, and other large structures help ground the description.

Duke Zalto is a visionary villain, not a mindless brute. Play him as someone who genuinely believes in what he is doing — he sees the Vonindod as a gift to his god and his people, a proof of fire giant superiority that will establish a new world order. His conviction should be unsettling because it is sincere. The moment when that conviction is challenged (if the party reveals Surtur's silence) should feel like watching a cathedral crack.

The moral choice regarding Maegera is the scenario's emotional climax, separate from the combat climax of fighting Zalto. Freeing Maegera is the easy way to destroy the Vonindod but comes with enormous collateral damage. The partial release is surgically precise but leaves the primordial still suffering. And leaving Maegera imprisoned while finding another way to stop Zalto is pragmatic but morally ambiguous. There is no right answer — let the party debate and honor their choice.

Track the freed captives and azers as narrative threads. The enslaved workers are not just set dressing — they are people with names, stories, and futures that depend on the party's actions. If the party takes time to free them, reward that heroism with information, assistance, and emotional payoff. If the party prioritizes speed over rescue, let the weight of that choice be felt without punishing the party mechanically.
